title: Capacity flipbook: token velocity vs salary spline
content:
Purpose:
Short working spreadsheet to map short-cycle token-demand surges to headcount gating and small price adjustments. Experimental — meant for planning the next 6 quarters with a rolling 12-week action window.

Executive summary:
- Build a small, calibrated headcount buffer aligned to token-velocity splines (spline = smoothed demand curve).
- Prioritize short-horizon hiring (contractor->perm) for inference ops and SRE.
- Use micro price nudges (0.5–3%) as the primary throttle before unlocking hires for persistent demand.

Key assumptions (configurable):
- Baseline token growth: 12% q/q organic; burst probability 18% per quarter.
- Average tokens/server-hour: 28M tokens / GPU-hour (post-quantization tuning).
- Latency SLO requires peak capacity headroom of 25% above P95 QPS.
- Average time-to-fill (perm infra role): 9 weeks; contractors: 2 weeks.
- Fully loaded annual cost per infra hire: $220k (salary + benefits + overhead).
- Spot/gpu-burst cost premium when bursting: +26% per token served.

Scenario table (quick view):
Columns: Scenario | Quarter growth | Peak weekly surge | Extra GPU-hrs needed | Net new hires (ops) | Hiring mix (perm:contract) | Immediate cost delta (monthly) | Recommended price nudge
1) Baseline steady: +12% | 3x baseline weekly | 0 | 0 | 0:0 | $0 | 0%
2) Micro-surge: +28% qtr | 5x weekly peak | 120 GPU-hrs | 1 | 0:1 | $14,000 | 0.5%
3) Sustained shift: +45% qtr | 8x weekly peak | 450 GPU-hrs | 3 | 2:1 | $55,000 | 1.2%
4) Demand shock: +90% qtr | 12x weekly peak | 1,250 GPU-hrs | 8 | 6:2 | $160,000 | 2.5–3.0%

Notes on numbers above: GPU-hrs = additional GPU-hours per peak week, computed using token/hr and average sequence length profiles. Immediate cost delta = incremental monthly burn from hiring and burst premiums. Price nudge = recommended immediate per-token price increase for new customers or temporary surcharge; applied progressively: 0.5% for micro-surge, up to 3% for shock.

Headcount phasing (rolling 12-week action windows):
- Weeks 0–2: Activate price nudge 0.5%, enable short-burst spot capacity, spin up contractors for 1–2 weeks to absorb spikes.
- Weeks 3–6: If surge persists above 4 weeks, start recruiting perm infra engineers (1–3 reqs) and add predictable dedicated GPUs.
- Weeks 7–12: On sustained demand, onboard perm hires, re-evaluate SLA cadence and consider +1.0–2.0% price step for affected route classes.

Discipline split for hires (recommended mix when adding perm roles):
- Serving runtime / inference ops: 45%
- Site Reliability / capacity orchestration: 30%
- Tools / cost engineering: 15%
- Product gating & billing analytics: 10%

Micropricing experiment matrix (A/B quick run):
- Treatment A: 0.5% across-the-board surcharge for top 20% token-consuming customers; monitor churn / usage elasticity for 4 weeks.
- Treatment B: Tiered surcharge (1% above 500k tokens/day) with credits for committed-run reservations.
- Metrics to capture: delta in token-hours, churn rate by cohort, incremental gross margin, impact on burst frequency.

Trigger rules (operational):
- Metric: 7-day rolling token-velocity crosses +35% vs baseline AND sustained for 5 days -> enable price nudge A and auto-burst to spot pool.
- Metric: 4-week cumulative extra GPU-hrs > 1,000 -> open hiring queue for 2 perm infra roles (SRE-focused).
- Metric: Customer concentration: top-5 customers account for >38% of burst increase -> engage Solutions/Account teams before perm hires.

Risk considerations and mitigations:
- Hiring lag vs demand speed: keep a 2-FTE contractor pool pre-approved for immediate spin-up.
- Churn risk from pricing: cap surcharge window to 12 weeks and provide reservation credits to largest customers.
- Capex vs opex balance: prefer short-term GPU spot bursts until 3 consecutive quarters validate persistent lift.

Small sensitivity matrix (toy):
- Vary token efficiency (±15%): if efficiency drops 15%, required GPU-hrs increase ~18% and hiring triggers move forward ~1 recruitment slot per sustained quarter.
- Vary hiring lag (6->12 wks): increases reliance on pricing levers and contractor hours; expected incremental monthly cost rises by ~22%.

Runbook checklist (actionable):
- [ ] Export P95 QPS by route -> confirm baseline token/hr inputs (owner: ops-analytics).
- [ ] Create contractor PO template (owner: finance-ops).
- [ ] Prepare pricing communication templates for 0.5% and 1.5% nudges (owner: GTM).
- [ ] Queue 2 infra reqs in ATS with accelerated timeline (owner: eng-recruiting).
- [ ] Instrument surge dashboard with spike-alert lambda (owner: observability team).

Open questions / data needs (notes to self):
- How correlated are bursts across regions? If uncorrelated, regional burst strategies change (less hiring, more regional routing).
- Get detailed token-per-customer distribution to calculate progressive surcharge cliffs that minimize churn risk.
- Validate GPU-hr assumptions with serving-runtime team after latest kernel optimizations (PR #284).

Appendix: quick cost math (for modelers)
- tokens_needed_per_week = baseline_weekly_tokens * surge_multiplier
- gpu_hours_needed = tokens_needed_per_week / tokens_per_gpu_hour
- estimated_hire_count = ceil(max(0, (gpu_hours_needed - available_buffer_hours) / hours_covered_by_one_engineer))
- hours_covered_by_one_engineer ~ 28 * 40 (conservative ops coverage factoring on-call)

Last notes: this is an intentionally compact, tactical doc — meant to be iterated quickly. Use the linked Confluence page for longer-term modeling and push any agreed trigger thresholds into the Alerting board.
